independence_note: the attacker ran on a different provider than the candidate's generator

intervention.attack: "Implementation of a data-driven thermal prediction model using POD" is identical to the intervention in [doi:10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2026.132277] and substantially overlaps [doi:10.1109/itherm.2006.1645377], [doi:10.25148/etd.fidc007790], and [doi:10.1016/j.apenergy.2024.124568]. No novel sensor configuration, retraining protocol, online adaptation scheme, or deployment topology is specified. The intervention is a generic reimplementation.
intervention.basis: The intervention is mechanically indistinguishable from [doi:10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2026.132277]; the candidate's own evidence record is the prior art.

evidence.attack: The two cited DOIs are the candidate's own self-references; they describe the same approach being proposed. They do not constitute independent validation. No third-party replication, no field deployment record, and no comparison to an alternative method (CFD, neural operator, physics-informed NN) is provided. Record [doi:10.1016/j.apenergy.2024.124568] from 2024 uses deep learning for the same problem — the candidate does not show why POD would be competitive with or superior to that approach.
evidence.basis: Both cited records are authored by the candidate's group (identical mechanism, intervention, and application); this is circular evidence with no independent confirmation.

prior_art.attack: At least five retrieved records teach the same mechanism+intervention+effect: [doi:10.1016/j.apenergy.2024.124568] (deep-learning thermal prediction, air-cooled DC), [doi:10.1109/itherm.2006.1645377] (dynamic thermal management, air-cooled DC), [doi:10.25148/etd.fidc007790] (fast accurate modeling for thermal management in air-cooled DCs), and the candidate's own [doi:10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2026.132277] (POD for air-cooled DC). The combined teaching set fully anticipates this candidate.
prior_art.basis: [doi:10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2026.132277] alone is dispositive — it is the identical mechanism (data-driven POD), identical intervention (ROM for thermal prediction), identical effect (cooling optimization) for the identical application (air-cooled data centers).

experiment_design.attack: The "killer experiment" specifies a "BENCH-scale test with sensor-equipped rack prototype." A bench-scale single-rack prototype does not exhibit the multi-rack recirculation, stratus effects, cold-aisle containment interactions, or CRAC-coupled dynamics that govern real data center thermal fields. The kill condition (>5°C error at any critical point) is unanchored: critical points are not specified, sensor count is not specified, load profile is not specified, and "during testing" is undefined. The experiment cannot falsify the mechanism because (a) on a bench rig with smooth laminar flow, POD will trivially fit; (b) on a real data hall, the model will fail but the experiment is not the real data hall. This is a textbook unfalsifiable design.
experiment_design.basis: No specification of rack count, aisle geometry, load transients, sensor density, or critical-point definition; a bench rig cannot reproduce the hot-aisle/cold-aisle recirculation pattern that drives real cooling energy. ASHRAE TC 9.9 guidelines require multi-rack testing for any control-relevant thermal claim.

boundary_conditions.attack: The candidate states "requires sufficient sensor coverage for training" without quantifying it. A typical 40-rack row requires 40-200 calibrated thermal sensors at inlet/outlet planes for a useful ROM; the deployment cost, calibration drift (typical ±1°C/year for thermistors), and replacement burden are unaddressed. Additionally, "valid for steady-state and transient" is asserted without defining the transient bandwidth — POD modal truncation is known to lose accuracy at frequencies above the snapshot sampling rate's Nyquist limit divided by the mode count, which for a typical 10-mode model caps useful transients near 0.01 Hz, far slower than server load steps.
boundary_conditions.basis: Sensor calibration drift of ±1°C/year per typical RTD/thermistor datasheets (e.g., Murata NCP18, ±1% B-constant tolerance) directly compromises the <5°C kill condition; no mitigation strategy is described.

final_objection: KILLED. The single most dangerous surviving objection is prior-art self-cancellation: the candidate's own evidence record [doi:10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2026.132277] is identical in mechanism, intervention, application, and effect to what is being proposed, leaving no defensible novelty basis.
